name: apply_patch
description: Apply localized edits from inline text or a patch file. Supports line replacement, patch envelopes, and unified diffs.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later patches in this turn:
- Copy source text exactly without `read_file` line prefixes; context lines must match.
- For a single-line change prefer `*** Replace in line:`: it matches no context, only `anchor:`/`old:`.
- When a hunk fails to match, the error echoes the current file text in a `<<<PATCH_TEXT` block; rebuild the patch from that block instead of re-reading the file.
- `*** Begin Patch` ... `*** End Patch` envelopes support `*** Update File:`, `*** Add File:` with `+`-prefixed content, and `*** Delete File:` plus `@@` hunks.
- Multi-file unified diffs split automatically, but unified diffs cannot delete files.

file_path.description: Absolute target for a single-file unified diff when its headers omit the file; `path` is an alias.

patch.description: Inline edit in exactly one form: `*** Replace in line: <path>` inside a `*** Begin Patch` envelope; an envelope with `*** Update/Add/Delete File:` sections and `@@` hunks; or a unified diff. No Markdown fences or no-op edits. `*** Replace in line:` takes exactly three single-line fields: `anchor:` (unique substring of the target line), `old:` (exact substring to replace), `new:` (replacement; empty deletes `old`); to insert or replace whole lines use a `*** Update File:` hunk with `@@`. Limit: 8000 characters - for larger edits use `patch_file` or split.

patch_file.description: Patch-file path instead of `patch`; must be session-temp or under the working directory. Mutually exclusive with `patch`; limit 64000 characters.
